slice: KTM 250 SX-F, Husqvarna FC 250, GasGas MC 250F 2023-2026 (current generation) with 2020-2022 summary; notes for KTM 250 XC-F and GasGas EX 250F (no Husqvarna FX 250 in the US)

records.statement: The 2023 KTM 250 SX-F and Husqvarna FC 250 started the current generation: a new short-stroke engine (81 x 48.5 mm instead of 78 x 52.3 mm), the new hydroformed chromoly frame shared with the 450, a new die-cast swingarm, a new WP shock and standard quickshifter. 2024-2026 are evolutions of that bike.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: Bore/stroke and frame details are KTM data repeated by the magazine; tier MEASURED used because the generation summary combines tester findings. Generation shared with Husqvarna FC 250 from 2023 and GasGas MC 250F from 2024.

records.statement: The mid-2022 KTM 250 SX-F Factory Edition was the first bike with the new engine and frame: 81 x 48.5 mm, compression up from 14.4 to 14.5:1, exhaust valves up from 26.5 to 27.5 mm, a lighter head, engine tilted 2 degrees back, 8 mm shorter engine, 3 mm lower countershaft sprocket, 22 mm rear axle (was 25 mm), new WP shock and quickshift.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2022-1/2 KTM 250SXF Factory Edition

records.notes: Magazine repeats KTM data. The article calls the old engine the '2013 engine'; the 78 x 52.3 mm engine actually ran 2016-2022 (MXA 2022 race test says the engine premiered in 2016).

records.statement: For 2023 nearly every engine part changed: bigger bore and shorter stroke allowing bigger ports, a lighter head, DOHC with DLC-coated finger followers, titanium valves (32.5 mm intake, 27.5 mm exhaust), a new 44 mm throttle body, an engine 8 mm shorter and tilted 2 degrees back, and new frame, swingarm, subframe, shock and bodywork shared with the 450.

source.name: Dirt Bike: 2023 KTM 250SX-F Full Test

records.notes: Valve sizes also in KTM 250 XC-F press text. Weight rose from 218 lb (2022) to 224-226 lb depending on scale.

records.topic: 2023 GasGas MC 250F stayed on old platform
records.statement: The 2023 GasGas MC 250F kept the 2022 frame, subframe and 78 x 52.3 mm engine; it moved to the new-generation engine and chassis for 2024. That made the 2023 GasGas the lightest bike in the class at 217 lb.

source.name: Motocross Action: 2023 250 Four-Stroke Shootout

records.notes: Weight on calibrated beam scale, empty fuel tank, all other fluids.

records.statement: 2024 was a carry-over year: new graphics, slightly smoother fork mid-valve compression, and the shock's high-speed compression shim stack grew from 15 to 23 shims, roughly halving the damping change per click. Husqvarna also got a redesigned shock preload collar and the KTM subframe design.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: Same changes listed for Husqvarna in the 2024 FC250 race test. KTM also lists a simplified map/TC switch and flatter seat.

records.statement: The mid-2024 Factory/Rockstar Editions previewed the 2025 frame (relief holes in the forged shock tower, hollowed head stays). The FC 250 Rockstar Edition had an FMF Factory 4.1 RCT titanium slip-on and the MC 250F Factory Edition an Akrapovic titanium slip-on, both with a one-piece intake sleeve and snorkel.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: Frame preview from the 2025 KTM race test; muffler details from Dirt Rider Rockstar and MC 250F FE dyno tests.

records.statement: For 2025 the frame kept its geometry but lost material for more flex: relief holes in the forged shock tower, hollowed head stays, thinner backbone plates and thinner-wall long tubes. The linkage arms got shorter and thinner with smaller bolts (17 to 15 mm and 17 to 14 mm), shock valving got slightly stiffer with low-stiction seals, the swingarm top was lowered with a raised buffer pad, traction control was improved and the rear brake pedal tip was strengthened.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: 2023-2024 aftermarket linkages do not fit 2025. 2024 radiator graphics do not fit 2025 shrouds. Testers felt the softer frame most in acceleration chop. MXA says KTM did not announce any mapping changes.

records.statement: 2026 changes to the standard 250 SX-F are minor: new in-mould graphics with a black powder-coated frame and black seat, an easier-to-open radiator cap, and a protector cap on the fuel-line quick connector. No engine, mapping or suspension changes were announced for the 250 SX-F.

source.name: Enduro21: First Look 2026 KTM SX and SX-F

records.notes: Price from Dirt Rider 2026 technical overview. KTM's 2026 Factory Edition page lists more (frame backbone change, linkage geometry, footpegs, chain guide) but those are described on the Factory Edition page only.

records.statement: The 2026 KTM 250 SX-F Factory Edition comes with WP XACT PRO 7548 closed-cartridge coil-spring forks and an XACT PRO 8950 shock, an updated Akrapovic titanium muffler with revised intake and mapping, a standard CUO connectivity unit, WP start device, factory triple clamps and wheels. KTM lists 105 kg without fuel and $12,599.

values.fork: WP XACT PRO 7548 48 mm closed cartridge

source.name: KTM USA 2026 250 SX-F Factory Edition page

records.notes: Standard 2026 250 SX-F keeps the WP XACT air fork (AER).

source.name: Motocross Action: 2025 250 Shootout

records.notes: Collected from MXA race tests/shootouts and Dirt Rider 2026 overview. Prices are MSRP without freight.

records.statement: The previous engine (78 x 52.3 mm, 14.4:1) ran from 2016 to 2022 and revved to about 14,000 rpm; stock gearing was 14/51 from 2017. 2020 brought WP XACT air forks and an optional vented airbox cover; 2022 swapped the counterbalancer needle bearing for a plain bushing and was otherwise a carry-over. It weighed 218 lb, among the lightest 250Fs.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2022 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: Combined from MXA 2020 and 2022 race tests. The engine won MXA's 250 shootout five times in six years (the 2021 loss was to the Husqvarna FC 250 with the same engine).

records.statement: The engine is 81.0 x 48.5 mm for 249.9 cc with 14.5:1 compression, a DOHC four-valve head, Keihin EFI with a 44 mm throttle body, a 5-speed gearbox (6-speed on XC-F/EX 250F) and an electric starter.

source.name: KTM 2024 250 SX-F model page

records.notes: Same on Husqvarna FC 250 (Motorcycle.com/Dirt Rider) and GasGas MC/EX 250F (Dirt Rider). KTM page claims 'over 47 hp' (crank figure, not wheel).

records.statement: KTM gives the maximum engine speed as 14,000 rpm. Testers say the engine revs to about 14,000 rpm and that the limiter is less abrupt than on the old engine.

source.name: KTM 2023 250 XC-F press text (reprinted by Total Motorcycle)

records.notes: Dirt Rider 2024 tech info also states 'up to 14,000 rpm'; Dirt Bike 2023 says it revs 'well over 13,000' with a softer limiter.

records.statement: The head uses DLC-coated finger followers and titanium valves: 32.5 mm intake and 27.5 mm exhaust. Finger followers are light, which lets the engine use aggressive cam profiles and rev high without the valves floating.

source.name: KTM 2023 250 XC-F press text (reprinted by Total Motorcycle)

records.notes: Valve sizes confirmed by Dirt Bike 2023 test and Dirt Rider 2024 tech info. Exhaust valve growth from MXA 2022.5 FE test.

records.statement: KTM lists a forged bridged-box piston by CP, a lightened crankshaft with a counterbalancer shaft, and a DS (diaphragm-steel) clutch with a one-piece steel basket and Brembo hydraulics.

source.name: KTM 2023 250 XC-F press text (reprinted by Total Motorcycle)

records.notes: Source is the 250 XC-F press text; the SX-F shares the engine. GasGas uses a Braktec hydraulic clutch actuation with the same internals.

records.statement: From 2023 the 44 mm throttle body has a double-injector layout and the throttle cable connects directly, without a throttle linkage.

source.name: KTM 2023 250 XC-F press text (reprinted by Total Motorcycle)

records.notes: Vortex ECU listing also mentions dual injector driver support for 2023+ 250s.

records.statement: The engine is tilted 2 degrees backward, is 8 mm shorter, and the countershaft sprocket sits 3 mm lower than before, which KTM says reduces squat under acceleration.

source.name: KTM 2024 250 SX-F model page

records.statement: All three use the same engine and ECU but breathe differently: the KTM has open vents in the subframe under the seat and an optional vented airbox cover, the Husqvarna has the vents moulded shut, and the GasGas has the most closed-off airbox cover. GasGas also has an extra baffle/restrictor in the muffler.

values.KTM: open subframe vents, optional vented cover
values.Husqvarna: vents moulded shut, optional vented cover

source.name: Motocross Action: 2025 250 Shootout

records.notes: MXA says KTM deliberately limits the Husqvarna's breathing to keep the brands distinct. The closed airboxes cost throttle response more than dyno peak numbers.

records.statement: Worked out from KTM's bore and stroke, the engine is strongly oversquare at 1.67:1, up from 1.49:1 on the 2016-2022 engine. A shorter stroke lets the engine spin faster for the same piston speed.

source.name: BAK MX calculation from published bore, stroke, rpm and dyno figures

records.statement: Worked out from the 48.5 mm stroke, mean piston speed is about 22.6 m/s at the 14,000 rpm limit and about 22.1 m/s at a 13,700 rpm power peak. The old 52.3 mm stroke engine reached about 24.4 m/s at the same 14,000 rpm, so the new engine is under less stress at the same revs.

source.name: BAK MX calculation from published bore, stroke, rpm and dyno figures

records.statement: Worked out from the published valve sizes, the two intake valve heads cover about 32% of the bore area and the two exhaust valves about 23%, which is the kind of large valve area that supports high-rpm breathing.

source.name: BAK MX calculation from published bore, stroke, rpm and dyno figures

records.notes: Area = pi/4 x d^2. Uses valve head diameter, not throat or curtain area, so it is only a rough breathing indicator.

records.statement: Worked out from the highest rear-wheel figure recorded (45.2 hp), the engine makes about 181 hp per litre at the wheel.

records.notes: 45.20 hp / 0.2499 L = 180.9 hp/L. Based on the MXA 2023-2024 dyno (Pro Circuit dyno for shootouts); other dynos read lower.

records.statement: On a magazine dyno the 2023 KTM 250 SX-F made 44.4 hp at 13,700 rpm versus 44.2 hp for the 2022, both peaking at 13,700 rpm. Up to 9,500 rpm they were within 0.3-0.5 hp; above 9,500 rpm the 2023 was about 1 hp stronger to the limiter.

records.notes: EX 250F figures from DREX24. Same engine as the SX-F; cross-country models have a 6-speed box.

records.statement: Rear-wheel peak figures for the same KTM 250 SX-F range from about 40 hp on one in-house Dynojet to about 45 hp on a race-shop dyno. Compare bikes only within one source and one test day.

source.name: Dirt Bike: 250 Motocross Bikes on the Dyno - The Wrap (2025)

records.notes: See conflicts. Differences come from dyno type, correction, tyre, temperature and fuel load.

records.statement: Testers describe a quiet, very linear engine: the bottom end feels less exciting than a Yamaha or Honda, it builds through a strong midrange, does its best work above about 11,000 rpm and keeps pulling to about 14,000 rpm where rivals have signed off. Because it is smooth and quiet it feels slower than the dyno shows.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: Same picture in MXA 2023/2024 race tests and 2023-2025 shootouts, Dirt Rider 2024-2025 ('shines at high rpm'), Dirt Bike 2023 ('very linear', 'rev it out').

records.topic: why it feels the way it does
records.statement: The short 48.5 mm stroke, light finger-follower valvetrain and big titanium valves let the engine breathe and rev to 14,000 rpm. Peak torque arrives around 9,200-9,600 rpm but peak power not until about 13,000-13,500 rpm, so power keeps rising for over 4,000 rpm after the torque peak. On the YZ250F that gap is under 2,800 rpm, which is why the Yamaha feels punchy and then signs off while the KTM feels flat but keeps pulling.

source.name: BAK MX calculation from published bore, stroke, rpm and dyno figures

records.notes: Gap computed from the 2025 Pro Circuit dyno figures (Dirt Bike): KTM 13,470 - 9,210 = 4,260 rpm; YZ250F 12,880 - 10,100 = 2,780 rpm. Architecture explanation combines KTM data (finger followers, valve sizes, 14,000 rpm) with testers' descriptions; the link between them is BAK's engineering reading.

records.statement: Most testers found the 2023 engine slightly less snappy off the bottom than the 2022 but stronger through the midrange and on top; one review instead found it noticeably punchier off the bottom in map 2. It still needs revs.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: Cycle News 2023 first ride called it punchier with a 'Japanese hit'; MXA and Dirt Bike called it similar or less snappy down low. Kept as a disagreement.

records.statement: One tester found the engine needs a big throttle opening: it out-ran the 2022 YZ250F at wide-open throttle but not at quarter or half throttle.

source.name: Dirt Bike: 2023 KTM 250SX-F Full Test

records.statement: Back-to-back, the Yamaha YZ250F feels stronger off the bottom because it is louder and pulls harder low down, the Honda CRF250R is livelier low but fades, the Kawasaki KX250 has a narrower window, and the Triumph TF 250-X has a low-midrange lull and a bog on a fast throttle opening. The Austrian 250s have the widest usable power window and pull away at the top of straights.

source.name: Motocross Action: 2025 250 Shootout

records.notes: Combined from MXA 2024 and 2025 shootouts and Cycle News 2025 shootout.

records.statement: The Husqvarna has the same engine but its closed airbox makes it slightly softer and smoother off the bottom; the KTM feels snappier on track. Once on the pipe it pulls hard from midrange and wants to be revved very high.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 Husqvarna FC250

records.notes: MXA 2023 found the Husky better than the KTM in some low-mid situations; Cycle News 2025 called its roll-on more manageable.

records.statement: The GasGas has a mellower bottom end and less excitement on top in stock form because of its closed airbox, muffler restrictor and single map. Some testers still found it the most fun of the three, coming alive quickly off the bottom with a connected midrange.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 GasGas MC250F

records.notes: Cycle News 2025 shootout voted it the most fun Austrian engine; MXA calls it 'sabotaged' by intake and exhaust restrictions. Kept as differing opinions.

records.statement: On a beam scale with an empty tank the KTM 250 SX-F weighed 218 lb in 2022 and 224 lb in 2023-2024 (about 1 lb less in 2025). The Husqvarna weighed 224 lb (2023-2024). The GasGas weighed 217 lb on the old platform (2023) and 225 lb from 2024.

source.name: Motocross Action: 2025 250 Shootout

records.notes: Empty fuel tank, all other fluids. Other scales: Dirt Bike 226 lb without fuel (2023); Dirt Rider 237 lb full tank (2024); Cycle News 2025 wet: KTM 236, FC 235, MC 238 lb.

records.topic: engine braking and over-rev on cross-country models
records.statement: The GasGas EX 250F's wide-ratio 6-speed makes the gaps between gears less noticeable; the power is described as long and linear with no hard hit, and slightly smoother than the MC 250F.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2024 GasGas EX 250F Dyno Test

records.notes: Engine braking behaviour not described by any source found.

records.statement: A left-bar switch selects two maps: map 1 has a more linear power curve and map 2 is more aggressive. The same switch turns traction control and the quickshifter on and off, and both buttons together arm launch control.

source.name: KTM 2024 250 SX-F model page

records.notes: A gear-position sensor lets the ECU run gear-specific maps (KTM 250 XC-F press text).

records.statement: Most testers race in the aggressive map (map 2, shown with a green light) because a 250 should not be detuned; the mellow map suits very light riders, novices or slick tracks. In 2023 the two maps were more different than before; earlier testers felt they were too similar.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 Husqvarna FC250

records.notes: MXA 2023 KTM/FC tests, Cycle News 2025 (green map preferred; FC testers preferred map 2) and MotoOnline 2024 all favour the aggressive map. MXA's 2024 KTM test labels the green map as 'map 1' - see conflicts.

records.statement: The standard US GasGas MC 250F has the same ECU and maps but no switch: it runs only map 1 with no traction control or quickshift until a Power Parts switch (about $180-200) is fitted.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 GasGas MC250F

records.notes: The 2024 Australian-market MC 250F tested by MotoOnline had the switch with two maps, TC and quickshift fitted, so equipment differs by market.

records.statement: Traction control watches how fast rpm rises; if revs climb too quickly (wheelspin) it retards ignition and cuts power. KTM suggests it for wet or muddy conditions.

source.name: KTM 2023 250 XC-F press text (reprinted by Total Motorcycle)

records.notes: Mechanism detail (ignition retard on runaway revs) from MXA 'what happens when I press the buttons' (2017 KTM), which describes it as closer to a third, hard-pack map than a factory-level TC system.

records.topic: traction control on the 250: tester advice
records.statement: On the 2023-2024 250s testers found traction control cut power by roughly 25%, made the engine sound rough or rich and was nearly unusable; most leave it off. The pre-2023 version was occasionally useful.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 Husqvarna FC250

records.notes: MXA 2023 KTM, 2023 FC, 2024 KTM, 2024 FC race tests all agree.

records.statement: Traction control was improved for 2025. Testers still rarely use it but say it helps on wet, muddy or rock-hard tracks, or for a light (about 130 lb) rider who wants calmer power.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.statement: Launch control is armed at idle by pressing the traction control and quickshift buttons together; it limits rear-wheel power off the start. On the older system, letting revs drop more than about 30% cancelled it until the engine was restarted.

values.arming: TC + QS buttons together at idle

source.name: KTM USA 2026 250 SX-F Factory Edition page

records.notes: The 30% figure comes from MXA describing a 2017 KTM; not confirmed for the 2023+ system. Testers rarely use launch control on dirt starts but do on concrete.

records.statement: The quickshifter allows clutchless full-throttle upshifts from 2nd to 5th by briefly cutting ignition. Most testers leave it off on the track and use it mainly for long, fast starts; it can be switched off with its button.

source.name: KTM 2024 250 SX-F model page

records.notes: Tester advice from MXA 2023-2024 KTM/FC race tests. The 450 gained two quickshifter reaction speeds for 2025; not confirmed for the 250.

records.statement: Factory Editions come with the CUO module, which links to the KTMconnect app to adjust ECU behaviour, show engine data and lap times and suggest suspension settings. GPS/transponder parts were sold separately for $249.99 in 2025 and fit 2023-2025 bikes.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: Standard on the 2026 Factory Edition per KTM. Adjustable parameters not listed for the 250 specifically; see ktm450sxf.json for the CUO parameter list.

records.statement: At launch the 2023 KTM 250 SX-F ECU was locked, so it could not be remapped by the usual flash services.

source.name: Motocross Action: 2023 250 Four-Stroke Shootout

records.notes: Listed as a negative in MXA's 2023 shootout. Later remap availability unclear (see Taco Moto record).

records.statement: A Vortex plug-in ECU is sold for 2023-2025 KTM 250 SX-F/XC-F, Husqvarna FC 250 and 2024-2025 GasGas MC 250F, with 10 base maps and support for the stock switch, traction control, launch control and quickshift; listed at $799.95 (was $1,049.95).

source.name: MX Locker listing: Vortex ECU 2023-2025 KTM 250 SX-F / Husqvarna FC 250 (Dynamic Engine Factory)

records.notes: Seller's claims (more bottom end, higher rev limit, better over-rev) are unverified; no dyno data found. Fitment table on the listing is inconsistent across years. Owners report older Vortex units may not support the 2023+ switch unless reprogrammed by XPR or Twisted Development (Vital MX, 350/450 owners).

records.statement: One stock-ECU remap service ($359, raises rev limit 500 rpm, gear-specific fuel and ignition) lists 2023+ 250 SX-F/FC 250/MC 250F only as 'coming soon'. The GET RX1 ECU listing covers enduro models but not the 250 SX-F.

source.name: Taco Moto: KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas stock ECU ship-in remapping service

records.notes: As of the 2025 page check, no confirmed stock-ECU remap for the 2023+ 250 SX-F was found. GET RX1 fitment from Rottweiler listing.

records.statement: Testers recommend KTM's optional vented airbox cover for sharper throttle response on the KTM and Husqvarna. On the 2020 bike it added only about 0.05 hp at peak but filled an 8,500-11,000 rpm dip.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2020 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: 2023-2025 race tests repeat the advice ('free power').

records.statement: To bring a GasGas MC 250F up to KTM feel: fit the map switch for map 2/TC/QS, drill or swap the airbox cover for more airflow, and replace the restricted muffler (an FMF muffler is suggested).

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 GasGas MC250F

records.notes: No before/after dyno published for these mods.

records.statement: Adding one tooth to the rear sprocket gives more low-rpm pull for riders who do not like to rev the engine; riders who stay high in the revs may not need it.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: On the 2020-2022 engine testers ran a 13-tooth countershaft (similar to +3 rear teeth) to cure sluggish turn exits. GasGas comes with one tooth more (52) than KTM.

records.statement: A Yoshimura RS-12 titanium system ($1,299) listed for the 2023 KTM 250 SX-F was only track-tested on a 350; no 250 dyno data was published.

source.name: Swapmoto Live: 2023 KTM 250 SX-F Yoshimura RS-12 titanium exhaust track test

records.notes: Included so the gap is visible; see not_found for 250 exhaust dynos.

records.statement: Special editions with titanium slip-ons (FMF Factory 4.1 RCT on the FC 250 Rockstar, Akrapovic on the MC 250F Factory Edition) did not show more peak power than standard bikes on one dyno: 40.6 hp and 40.2 hp versus 42.9 hp and 41.9 hp for the standard 2024 FC 250 and MC 250F.

source.name: Dirt Rider: 2024 Husqvarna FC 250 Rockstar Edition Dyno Test

records.notes: Same Dynojet 250i but different test days, so not a controlled before/after test.

records.statement: KTM lists a 63.9 degree steering head angle, 1,493 mm wheelbase, 958 mm seat height and 359 mm ground clearance, with a central double-cradle 25CrMo4 steel frame and aluminium-reinforced polyamide subframe.

source.name: KTM 2024 250 SX-F model page

records.notes: KTM's 2026 spec page lists 343 mm ground clearance and 101 kg without fuel; see conflicts. Triple clamp offset not found.

records.statement: KTM lists the 2026 250 SX-F at 101 kg without fuel, 958 mm seat height, 343 mm ground clearance, 7.2 L tank, 310 mm front and 300 mm rear travel, WP XACT AER 48 mm air fork, 24:72 primary drive and non-sealed 520 chain.

source.name: KTM USA 2026 250 SX-F technical specifications

records.statement: The Husqvarna sits about 1 inch lower than the KTM: forks 10 mm shorter, longer shock linkage arms and a taller shock seal head, with less rear travel (about 293 mm). It also has CNC triple clamps, ProTaper bars and its own plastics and frame colour.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 Husqvarna FC250

records.notes: Travel/seat/wheelbase from Motorcycle.com spec database (2024 FC 250); rake from Dirt Rider 2025 overview. Husqvarna officially says 10 mm lower.

records.statement: The GasGas uses the same frame (red) but forged aluminium triple clamps that flex more than KTM's CNC clamps, unbranded Neken bars 12 mm taller (Renthal 928-like bend), a slightly larger tank, its own subframe panels and seat mount, Braktec brakes and clutch hydraulics, Maxxis MX-ST tyres and a 52-tooth rear sprocket.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 GasGas MC250F

records.statement: The 2023+ frame squats less under power and pitches less under braking, absorbs braking and acceleration bumps better and is very stable, but felt stiff and harsh until about 8-10 hours of riding. The KTM suits faster riders and jumpy tracks; the lower Husqvarna turns tighter and suits shorter, lighter and novice-to-vet riders.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 Husqvarna FC250

records.notes: 2025 frame cut-outs reduced the harshness in chop.

records.statement: Frame history: 2023 new hydroformed chromoly frame with the backbone disconnected from the top shock mount and forged shock towers; 2025 relief holes in the shock tower, hollowed head stays and thinner tubes for more flex; 2026 Factory Edition gets a changed backbone and revised linkage geometry for ground clearance.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: 2026 FE detail from KTM's Factory Edition page.

records.statement: All three use the 48 mm WP XACT AER air fork (hydrostops from 2023) and a WP XACT shock with tool-free high/low-speed compression; the shock rebound adjuster is hard to reach and needs a flat screwdriver. Stock shock spring is 42 N/mm.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: KTM 250 XC-F and GasGas EX 250F use a coil-spring XACT fork with softer settings (Dirt Rider 2025 XC-F).

records.statement: The air fork's spring rate is set with a pump (stock about 10.7 bar / 155 psi). Pressure rises in the sun and while riding, so set it cold before riding and bleed the air screws each morning; a 5 psi change is clearly noticeable.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: 5 psi sensitivity from MotoOnline 2024 GasGas test.

records.statement: The GasGas has softer valving with less hold-up than the KTM; it works on rough tracks for vets and novices, but faster riders on jumpy tracks prefer KTM valving. Husqvarna valving was judged too soft for serious racers in 2023.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 GasGas MC250F

records.statement: Testers felt the 2023 shock's rising rate was not firm enough at the very end of the stroke; adding low-speed compression controls it. If the shock picks up speed at the end of its stroke, add low-speed compression.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 Husqvarna FC250

records.statement: Testers say air forks do things cartridge kits cannot and come free, while coil-spring kits give better hand comfort and ground-following and need no pressure checks. Options named include Dal Soggio Sphere FSR-48, Ohlins RXF 48S, WP 6500 cartridge and Kayaba coil kits at about $2,000-7,000.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.statement: Needle bearings can walk out of the linkage bell crank and bind it, making the rear feel dead (2 of 6 test bikes in one test). Check each slot; the fix is caged bearing KTM part 58033097000.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 Husqvarna FC250

records.notes: Also in MXA 2023 KTM race test.

records.statement: Spokes loosen quickly during break-in (up to about 6 hours to settle), starting with the ones next to the rear rim lock. Torque them before the first moto and check after every moto; check sprocket bolts too.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: Reported every year 2020-2025.

records.statement: The plastic minicycle-style radiator cap is hard to remove, has come off in a crash and is reported to leak; the factory team runs the older-style cap and a removal tool is sold. KTM changed the closure for 2026 to open with less force.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.statement: With the lower countershaft sprocket the chain wears the swingarm buffer pad quickly; testers fit a TM Designworks pad. For 2025 the pad was raised and the swingarm top lowered. Keep chain slack around 65-70 mm at the buffer pad, which looks loose.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: In 2022 KTM engineers told MXA 70 mm despite a 58 mm manual figure.

records.statement: The rear brake pedal tip bent or broke in crashes on 2023-2024 bikes (fixed for 2025). The low-profile start/stop and map buttons are hard to press with gloves; aftermarket kits relocate the kill button.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 KTM 250SXF

records.statement: Front Braktec brakes on 2022-2025 GasGas models are under recall. Testers also find Braktec brakes less precise than Brembo, and the Braktec clutch can surge when fanned or held at high rpm.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2025 GasGas MC250F

records.notes: Recall scope as reported by MXA; check the official recall notice by VIN.

records.statement: The one-piece GasGas airbox side panel fits loosely and has fallen off on the track when caught by a boot.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 GasGas MC250F

records.statement: Some owners report 2023+ 250s that become hard to start cold, blamed on a stuck piston ring (usually fixed with a new piston and ring) or tightening valve clearances; a leak-down test is advised over a compression test because of the auto-decompressor.

source.name: Vital MX forum: 23 KTM 250 SXF compression test

records.notes: Few reports; one owner says 2023 250s are 'notorious' for it. One FC 250 at 74 h read 50 psi on a compression test (conditions unknown). Not confirmed by any magazine or bulletin.

records.statement: On the 2020-2022 bikes the counterbalancer needle bearing could walk out (changed to a bushing for 2022), and sprocket bolts, head-stay bolts, lower subframe bolts and the linkage nut could loosen.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2022 KTM 250SXF

records.statement: One tester's baseline: fork 10.6 bar (10.5 for break-in), 5 mm fork height, 12 clicks out compression (or 15 out at 10.7 bar), 10 out rebound; shock 42 N/mm, 102 mm sag, 1.75 turns out high-speed, 10 out low-speed compression, 11 out rebound. Riders under 150 lb try about 10.3 bar.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing: 2023 250 MX Baseline Settings

records.notes: Fork needs 6-7 engine hours to break in.

records.statement: One tester's baseline: fork 10.7 bar, 5 mm height, 14 out compression, 9 out rebound; shock 42 N/mm, 102 mm sag, 1.5-1.75 turns out high-speed, 10 out low-speed, 11 out rebound. Set slightly stiffer than the KTM because the Husqvarna sits lower; 1.75 turns on high-speed helps front-end bite.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing: 2023 250 MX Baseline Settings

records.statement: One tester's baseline (old-platform 2023 bike): fork 10.6 bar, 5 mm height, 12 out compression, 10 out rebound; shock 42 N/mm, 102-103 mm sag, 1.75-2 turns out high-speed, 11 out low-speed, 11 out rebound.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Testing: 2023 250 MX Baseline Settings

records.statement: One magazine's race setup: fork 155 psi (stock 10.7 bar), 12 out compression, 18 out rebound, second line; shock 45 N/mm for riders 175 lb and over or 42 N/mm under 175 lb, 105 mm race sag (100-108 mm used), 12 out low-speed, 1.5 turns out high-speed, 14 out rebound. Set a fork zip tie about 1.5 in from bottoming.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: Tier MEASURED as magazine tester setup.

records.statement: One magazine's race setup: fork 156 psi (10.8 bar), 9 out compression (stock 12), 16 out rebound (stock 18), second line; shock 45 N/mm for 175 lb+ or 42 N/mm, 105 mm sag, 8 out low-speed (stock 12), 1.5 turns high-speed, 14 out rebound.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2023 Husqvarna FC250

records.notes: Stiffer low-speed used to control end-stroke drop. Same numbers given for the 2022-1/2 KTM FE.

records.statement: Previous-generation race setups: 2022 fork 152 psi, 10 out compression, 15 out rebound, third line; shock 45 N/mm, 106 mm sag, 2 turns high-speed, 15 out low-speed and rebound. 2020: fork 149 psi, 15 out both, third line; shock 42 N/mm, 105 mm sag, 2 turns high-speed, 15 out low-speed and rebound.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2022 KTM 250SXF

records.notes: 2020 numbers from MXA20.

records.statement: On the 2020-2022 bike (stock 14/51) fast testers ran 14/53 or 13/50, novice and vet testers preferred 14/52, and a 13-tooth countershaft cured the sluggish feel out of tight turns.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2020 KTM 250SXF

records.statement: The stock 42 N/mm shock spring suits riders under about 175 lb; heavier intermediate and pro riders should go to 45 N/mm.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 KTM 250SXF

records.statement: Typical tester recipe: race the aggressive map with traction control off, fit the vented airbox cover, rev the engine rather than short-shift (or add a rear tooth if you will not), start from stock clickers with 105 mm sag, check fork air before every ride and tighten spokes after every moto during break-in.

source.name: Motocross Action: MXA Race Test 2024 KTM 250SXF

records.statement: In one magazine's shootouts the KTM 250 SX-F won three years running (2023-2025) with the Husqvarna FC 250 second each year; the GasGas was 4th (2023) and 3rd (2024-2025). Another 2025 shootout put the YZ250F first, KTM 2nd, TF 250-X 3rd, CRF250R 4th, Husqvarna 5th and GasGas 6th, marking the Austrians down on price, the lowered Husqvarna chassis and GasGas brakes and suspension.

conflicts.topic: which map is the aggressive 'green' map
conflicts.note: Likely a labelling error in one article; OEM and most testers agree the aggressive map is map 2.
Different dynos and days; never average. Dirt Rider's Dynojet reads 3-5 hp lower than the race-shop dyno.
